parts.text:
The task is to set up a new Maven Spring Boot Java project with testing support: mocking, assertions, and loading Spring context.

The testing dependencies needed:
- Mocking: Mockito (spring-boot-starter-test includes mockito-core)
- Assertions: AssertJ (included in spring-boot-starter-test), JUnit Jupiter
- Loading Spring context: spring-boot-starter-test with @SpringBootTest

`spring-boot-starter-test` provides JUnit Jupiter, Mockito, AssertJ, Hamcrest, Spring Test, JSONassert, JsonPath.

Let me create the project structure. I don't have Java/Maven installed, so I can't verify build. But I'll create a proper project.

Let me decide versions. Today's date in env is Sep 2026, but let me use a stable, well-known version. Spring Boot 3.3.x requires Java 17+. Let me use Spring Boot 3.3.5 or 3.4.x. To be safe, I'll use a recent stable release. Given knowledge cutoff, Spring Boot 3.3.x/3.4.x are stable. I'll use 3.4.1 perhaps. But since I can't verify, maybe use 3.3.5 which is definitely available. Actually let me think about what's safest. Spring Boot 3.2.x/3.3.x are widely available. I'll go with 3.3.5 and Java 17.

Actually, let me consider whether network access is available to verify. Java/mvn are not installed. I could potentially install, but that's heavy. Let me just create the project files.

Let me set up:
```
pom.xml
src/main/java/com/example/demo/DemoApplication.java
src/main/java/com/example/demo/GreetingService.java (something testable)
src/test/java/com/example/demo/DemoApplicationTests.java (@SpringBootTest context load)
src/test/java/com/example/demo/GreetingServiceTest.java (Mockito mocking + AssertJ assertions)
```

The user said "needs testing support - mocking, assertions, and loading the Spring context - for its test suite." The main deliverable is the pom with dependencies and example tests demonstrating each.

Let me create a Spring Boot app. I'll use groupId com.example, artifactId demo.

Let me write the pom.xml.

Dependencies:
- spring-boot-starter (or web)
- spring-boot-starter-test (test scope)
- mockito-core is included but the task explicitly says mocking. I can add mockito-junit-jupiter explicitly? It's included in starter-test. But to be explicit about "mocking support", I could add `org.mockito:mockito-core` and `mockito-junit-jupiter` with managed versions. Actually spring-boot-starter-test already includes mockito-core and mockito-junit-jupiter. I'll rely on starter-test but maybe note it. The task wants mocking, assertions, loading context. spring-boot-starter-test covers all three: Mockito, AssertJ, Spring Test.

I'll keep it clean using the starter-test.

Let me create a service with a dependency to mock.

Design:
- `GreetingRepository` interface
- `GreetingService` depends on GreetingRepository
- `GreetingController`? Not needed.

Test:
- GreetingServiceTest uses @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class), @Mock GreetingRepository, @InjectMocks GreetingService, AssertJ assertions, verify.
- DemoApplicationTests uses @SpringBootTest for context loading.

Let me write these files. Include no comments per instructions (DO NOT ADD ANY COMMENTS unless asked). Hmm, that's a code style rule. But scaffolding often has comments. The instruction says do not add comments. I'll avoid comments in Java code.

Let me create files.
